title: Gideon and the Room
premise: Tamsin Villalobos returns to the family house in Hollow Creek to bury her twin brother Gideon, only to discover the body in the casket is not him — and that Gideon may still be somewhere inside the house's sealed back room, kept alive by a founders' ritual that trades one twin for the town's safety. Using old sleep recordings, Tamsin hears a second voice answering questions in Gideon's cadence and realizes the ritual is fraying: the room has begun taking memories as payment. To free her brother she must complete what the founders started — naming every debt the town owes — before the next new moon, when the room will claim a replacement permanently. In the end, Gideon chooses to stay so Tamsin can leave with the truth, but she refuses the choice the founders designed, sealing herself into the recording loop instead, leaving both twins half-present and the town finally forced to remember.
about_author: Y. M. Okafor is the pen name of a Nigerian-British writer who grew up between Lagos and Leeds, collecting family ghost stories the way other children collected stamps. Their fiction explores grief, inheritance, and the houses that keep both.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Tamsin Villalobos arrives in Hollow Creek for the funeral and lifts the casket lid against her mother's warnings; the face inside is Gideon's but the hands are wrong, too smooth, unscarred. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: dread disguised as grief, the first crack in certainty.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: Tamsin moves into the family house and falls into Gideon's old habits — counting doors each night, keeping lights on. She finds his notebook of sleep recordings labeled with dates after his supposed death. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: uncanny domesticity, love expressed as vigilance.

chapters.title: Static Answers
chapters.summary: Playing the recordings at 3 a.m., Tamsin hears an interviewer ask questions and a second voice — Gideon's, but flattened — answer about 'the room' and 'the debt.' The final tape addresses her by name. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Founders Kept
chapters.summary: In the historical society archive, Tamsin learns the town's founding families bound something beneath the Villalobos house, paid annually with a twin-born memory. The archivist, Mrs. Adeyemi, warns her to stop asking. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the horror of inherited obligation.

chapters.title: The Sealed Room
chapters.summary: Tamsin finds the back room behind Gideon's closet wall — cold, windowless, its door counted twice on every list he ever made. Scratched inside: tally marks and the words WE ANSWER SO YOU SLEEP. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: confrontation with the literal center of the mystery.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Words
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts her mother, Odile, who admits the family has fed the room for four generations and that Gideon went willingly to spare Tamsin, who was the intended payment. POV: alternating Tamsin and Odile. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with protective love.

chapters.title: Gideon Speaks
chapters.summary: Through the wall, Tamsin speaks with Gideon directly; he is lucid but losing memories in order — first their childhood dog, then their father's face. He begs her to let the ritual finish. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: heartbreak; duty versus devotion made intimate.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Tamsin canvases neighbors and finds systematic gaps: no one remembers 1974, or the first Villalobos twins. Mrs. Adeyemi slips her the founders' ledger before the archive burns that night. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: isolation deepening; loyalty to truth over community.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: The ledger lists every payment since 1891 — names, memories taken, and a final page: COMPLETION REQUIRES A VOLUNTARY WITNESS WHO REMEMBERS ALL. Tamsin realizes finishing the ritual could free Gideon or erase them both. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile reveals she was meant to be the witness thirty years ago and fled, which is why payments have grown crueler; the room punishes incomplete rituals. She begs Tamsin to run. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: guilt, maternal fear, the cost of cowardice.

chapters.title: The Interviewer
chapters.summary: Tamsin identifies the voice on the tapes: Elias Thorn, last living founder's descendant, who has been 'interviewing' the room for decades to keep it docile. He offers to train her as witness — for a price. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance, manipulation dressed as mentorship.

chapters.title: Lessons in Remembering
chapters.summary: Thorn drills Tamsin in mnemonic rites while the room grows restless — lights fail, doors multiply overnight, neighbors dream of Gideon calling. Her own memories begin thinning at the edges. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: racing clock, self-erosion.

chapters.title: New Moon Eve
chapters.summary: Preparations: salt lines, the ledger open, Odile standing guard outside despite her terror. Gideon tells Tamsin through the wall that if she enters, the room will offer her a bargain she must refuse. POV: alternating siblings. Emotional beat: calm before sacrifice.

chapters.title: Inside
chapters.summary: Tamsin crosses the threshold. The room is her childhood home endlessly repeated, and the thing within wears the faces of every forgotten founder. It shows her the original bargain: the town sleeps safe because one twin always remembers alone. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: The room offers Tamsin Gideon's freedom if she surrenders all memory of him — he would live, never knowing her. Gideon, present now in the room's flesh, screams at her to take the deal. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the thematic crux — love against duty, loyalty against truth.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Tamsin refuses and instead recites the full ledger aloud, forcing the room to hold every debt at once. The founders' binding cracks; Thorn, arriving to claim control, is pulled under as the room takes its overdue payment from its maker's line. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: defiant climax, terrible victory.

chapters.title: Half-Present
chapters.summary: Dawn. The room is gone, replaced by an ordinary wall — but Gideon remains as a presence in reflections and recordings, and Tamsin finds pieces of her own memory lodged in his voice. They are split across the threshold neither fully here nor gone. POV: alternating siblings. Emotional beat: bittersweet aftermath.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: With the binding broken, Hollow Creek's stolen decades flood back — funerals unheld, names unsaid. Some residents thank Tamsin; others blame her for the grief returned. Odile finally mourns her own lost twin. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: communal reckoning, truth's double edge.

chapters.title: Recording Again
chapters.summary: Tamsin sets up Gideon's old recorder and begins taping their conversations, building an archive so neither twin's memories can be lost again. His voice grows steadier; hers carries static now. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: tenderness rebuilt on new terms.

chapters.title: Doors, Counted
chapters.summary: A year later, Tamsin keeps the lights on out of habit, not fear. A child in town asks about the house with two people in it. Tamsin answers honestly. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: quiet normalization of the strange; grief integrated.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Final recording: an interviewer's question plays from nowhere, and both twins answer together, in unison, from either side of the wall. The tape ends mid-sentence, as if someone else is still listening. POV: none — pure document. Emotional beat: lingering unease, love persisting past the boundary.

chapters.title: We Answer So You Sleep
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Mrs. Adeyemi, alive and changed, opens a new archive with the ledger's blank final page filled in — TAMSIN AND GIDEON VILLALOBOS, WITNESSES, BOTH. Somewhere, a door counts itself. POV: omniscient. Emotional beat: resolution with a held breath; the story ends but the listening doesn't.
